newsitem.title: LATVIA: Estonian surge grabs Baltic market limelight.
newsitem.headline: Estonian surge grabs Baltic market limelight.

text.p: Estonia's market resumed its record-smashing bull run this week after a brief bout of profit-taking and further gains were seen ahead of profit forecast revisions in key banking stocks.
In Latvia, market leader Unibanka eased on news that the government would auction one million of its shares in the bank on July 28 at a minimum price of 3.05 lats.
Lithuania's bourse was mixed, as investors opted for the safety of leading blue chips. The rest of the market maintained its steady slide.
ESTONIA

Estonia's market caught its breath as players scooped up profits at the start of the week before rebounding to new highs. The Talse index rose to a record of 322.86 on Thursday from 310.46 the previous Thursday.

On Wednesday, record turnover of 178.8 million kroons ($12.5 million) was reached as the Norma Group sold 11.9 percent of its stake in its daughter company Norma, a diversified industrial firm, to western institutional investors in a deal worth 121 million kroons.
While shares across Europe soared this week, dealers and analysts said the market was responding to domestic stimuli and was not mirroring trends elsewhere.
"The market is still being pushed up by better than expected interim results in the banking sector," said one dealer.

Dealers said the market may take a breather next week but expect it to take off again at the end of the month when market leaders Hansapank and Hoiupank release their revised profit forecasts for the year.
In the medium-term, analysts say that Estonia's selection by the European Commission this week to be included in the first wave of EU entry talks will attract outside investment.
"It is a clear vote of confidence in Estonia's market reforms, and shows outside investors that the country is moving toward EU legal standards," said one dealer.
LATVIA

Activity was injected into Latvia's struggling market this week as investors snapped up shares in Unibanka, which began sliding last Friday after the privatisation agency announced that a big chunk of the state's stake in the bank would be sold at a minimum price of 3.05 lats.
Unibanka fell from 3.36 lats to 3.10 lats before rallying on Wednesday on Thursday, when it closed at 3.13 lats.
Dealers speculated that someone was supporting the price.
Unibanka's fall boosted volume but brought the bourse index down. It dropped to 376.95 on Thursday from 385.78 the previous Thursday.
But other shares picked up as interim results began trickling out and dealers say that short-term gains are on the horizon.
LITHUANIA

Investors in Vilnius took refuge in leading blue chips, boosting the five-stock official list to 939.64 on Thursday compared to 922.6 a week before. But the broader A list index fell to 1838.24 from 1870.89.
Dealers say local buyers have been wary since a long-term correction set in after a rapid surge in January and prefer safe bets such as leading banks Vilniaus and Hermis.
Hermis Bank gained to 210 litas from 200 litas over the week.
Vilniaus Bank gained only slightly over the week, rising to 245 litas from 240 litas despite a better than expected six-month profit result.
Dealers said the bank was looking a bit overpriced before the release of the results, which justified its price, but were not expected to push it up very much.
-- Riga newsroom +371 722 66 93 ($ = 14.34 Estonian Kroons)
